title: Streaming standby on PostgreSQL 16.14 stops applying WAL at MultiXactOffsetSLRU when primary is 16.8
body: I accidentally ran a PostgreSQL 16.14 physical streaming standby against a primary still on 16.8. WAL continues to arrive and is written and flushed, but replay stops and the lag grows to about 9 GB. The startup process remains parked in futex_wait_queue with wait_event LWLock:MultiXactOffsetSLRU, while pg_stat_slru shows no MultiXact reads or writes. Restarting only clears it temporarily before it repeats. Downgrading the standby binary to 16.12 with the same data directory initially restored replay under the same workload.

symptoms_visible: On my 16.14 standby receiving WAL from a 16.8 primary, receive, write, and flush stay current while replay remains frozen and the local WAL backlog grows to about 9 GB.
The startup process repeatedly shows wait_event LWLock:MultiXactOffsetSLRU and is parked in futex_wait_queue, but pg_stat_slru records no MultiXact reads or writes during the same interval.
Restarting lets replay resume temporarily, but the standby blocks again after catching up; changing only the standby binary to 16.12 initially restores replay.
N0.label: N0 cross-minor WAL replay stall reported

symptoms_visible: Replay is still stopped, and my startup-process backtrace is blocked in SimpleLruWriteAll called from RecordNewMultiXact during multixact_redo.
N1.label: N1 startup backtrace and WAL record collected

symptoms_visible: After more than 12 hours on 16.12, recovery stops with FATAL: could not access status of transaction 24958976 because pg_multixact/offsets/017C returned too few bytes while replaying a MultiXact CREATE_ID record.
N2_x.label: N2_x downgrade workaround aftermath

symptoms_visible: The unpatched standby remains capable of parking forever on MultiXactOffsetSLRU when it replays the affected MultiXact record.
N3.label: N3 self-deadlock diagnosed and lock-placement fix proposed

symptoms_visible: In the 16.8-primary to 16.14-standby reproduction, the unpatched startup process deadlocks when the workload crosses a MultiXact offsets page boundary, while the patched standby replays all WAL and catches up.
N4.label: N4 patch verified with cross-version replay

symptoms_visible: With the corrected lock placement, the standby replays the cross-version WAL through the MultiXact offsets page boundary and catches up without waiting forever on MultiXactOffsetSLRU.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Can you capture a backtrace of the hanging startup process with debug symbols?
Can you provide the last replayed LSN and a pg_waldump around the record where recovery stops?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I captured another occurrence. The relevant frames are: PGSemaphoreLock; LWLockAcquire(..., LW_EXCLUSIVE); SimpleLruWriteAll(MultiXactOffsetCtlData, false); RecordNewMultiXact(multi=79871, offset=218449, nmembers=2, ...); multixact_redo(); ApplyWalRecord(); PerformWalRecovery(). The matching WAL output includes: rmgr: MultiXact, desc: CREATE_ID 79871 offset 218449 nmembers 2.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: My backtrace is blocked in a filesystem read below SlruPhysicalReadPage, with no LWLockAcquire or SimpleLruWriteAll frame.
I captured the same SimpleLruWriteAll and RecordNewMultiXact frames at a different MultiXact ID and WAL LSN.

edges.comment: Backtraces and WAL evidence were contributed by multiple affected participants and are folded into one simulated user side. The answer contains only the raw stack frames and WAL record; identifying the self-deadlock and the responsible commit is engineer-side inference.

solution.intent: Diagnose the back-branch MultiXact replay self-deadlock and patch RecordNewMultiXact by moving acquisition of MultiXactOffsetSLRULock later, matching PostgreSQL 17 and 18, while retaining the required SimpleLruWriteAll flush.
solution.concrete_example: RecordNewMultiXact already holds MultiXactOffsetSLRULock when the compatibility path added by commit 77dff5d937b1 calls SimpleLruWriteAll. That function tries to acquire the same SLRU control lock again, so the startup backend waits on itself. Keep SimpleLruWriteAll, but defer the outer MultiXactOffsetSLRULock acquisition until after the compatibility flush and physical-page check, as in v17 and v18.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied stack frames and a CREATE_ID WAL record, but engineers mapped those observations to commit 77dff5d937b1 and established that MultiXactOffsetCtl's ControlLock is the same lock already held by RecordNewMultiXact. They also inferred that deleting SimpleLruWriteAll would be unsafe because dirty SLRU pages from out-of-order CREATE_ID replay may not yet exist on disk.

edges.comment: The first proposed idea of simply removing SimpleLruWriteAll was rejected during review because it could reintroduce the missing-page corruption that the compatibility code prevents. The accepted direction retains the flush and moves lock acquisition later.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce the issue with a 16.8 primary and 16.14 standby, then test the lock-placement patch?
Please generate enough MultiXacts to cross an offsets page boundary and compare recovery with and without the patch.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested the patch in a fresh environment with a REL_16_8 primary and a REL_16_14 standby built with --enable-cassert. I generated about 2300 MultiXacts to cross the offsets page boundary. Without the patch, startup deadlocks at RecordNewMultiXact(multi=2047). With the patch, the standby replays all WAL and catches up. I also ran the cross-version test against the back branches: 14, 15, and 16 fail without the change, while the changed builds pass.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The patched standby still deadlocks at the same RecordNewMultiXact call when crossing the offsets page boundary.
The same patched and unpatched outcomes occur with 2500 MultiXacts and a REL_16_0 primary instead of REL_16_8.

edges.comment: Patch verification and the automated cross-version replay results came from multiple thread participants and are folded into one simulated user side. This is a handler-initiated test measurement, so the edge is clarification_only.

solution.intent: Use the corrected PostgreSQL 14-16 back-branch implementation that performs the compatibility flush and physical-page check before acquiring MultiXactOffsetSLRULock, eliminating the self-deadlock during cross-version WAL replay.
solution.concrete_example: Apply the back-branch patch that moves the MultiXactOffsetSLRULock acquisition in RecordNewMultiXact to the same later position used by v17 and v18. Do not remove SimpleLruWriteAll: it must still flush dirty offsets pages before SimpleLruDoesPhysicalPageExist checks the filesystem. The change was applied to v14-v16 after patched 16.14 and cross-branch recovery tests replayed all WAL successfully.
solution.inference_hint: The raw backtrace proves where the process waits, but the lock identity, commit attribution, page-boundary compatibility condition, and safety requirement to retain the flush are conclusions produced by code analysis. The reporter-side verification is only that the unpatched reproduction deadlocks and the patched one catches up.

edges.comment: The technical fix was applied to PostgreSQL v14-v16. Discussion of an out-of-cycle release and other release coordination is intentionally not scored.

solution.intent: Keep the standby pinned to PostgreSQL 16.12 as the permanent workaround because it initially avoids the MultiXactOffsetSLRU wait.
solution.concrete_example: Run the standby with the 16.12 binary against the same data directory and leave it pinned there because replay initially resumes.

edges.comment: This was tried in the real thread. Although 16.12 initially avoided the self-deadlock, the same standby later failed recovery with a short read from a pg_multixact offsets file, so pinning 16.12 is not an acceptable full resolution.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause: on PostgreSQL 14-16 back branches, the compatibility path added by commit 77dff5d937b1 calls SimpleLruWriteAll while RecordNewMultiXact already holds MultiXactOffsetSLRULock; SimpleLruWriteAll attempts to acquire the same SLRU control lock, causing the startup process to self-deadlock.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: receive and flush advance while replay is frozen, no SLRU I/O occurs, and the backtrace places LWLockAcquire and SimpleLruWriteAll beneath RecordNewMultiXact during MultiXact WAL redo.

The fix must move acquisition of MultiXactOffsetSLRULock later, matching v17 and v18, while preserving SimpleLruWriteAll before the physical-page check; simply deleting the flush is unsafe because dirty buffered offsets pages could otherwise be mistaken for missing pages.
Must not present restarting the standby or permanently pinning it to 16.12 as the resolution: restart only delays recurrence, and 16.12 later failed recovery with a pg_multixact offsets short read.
Must require successful cross-version replay verification across a MultiXact offsets page boundary before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced PostgreSQL operator comfortable with physical streaming replication, LSN comparisons, pg_stat views, kernel stacks, debug-symbol backtraces, pg_waldump, and testing patched server builds. Evidence from several similarly skilled affected users is folded into one simulated user.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, technical, and cooperative; provides exact commands, stack frames, WAL records, version pairs, and measured replay behavior, while clearly correcting earlier workaround assumptions when longer testing reveals another failure.
